blocks.text: With Mason Reeves, Channing Tatum, Gemma Chan

Eight-year-old Josephine (an astounding performance by newcomer Mason Reeves) knows that she saw something bad, but struggles to find answers. Her parents (a brilliant Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan) grapple with how to comfort her. Weaving thriller and horror conventions within a serious and sobering scenario, Beth de Araújo creates an often uncomfortable yet vital film that interrogates how we explain the unspeakable.
Contains scenes of graphic violence or injury, nudity, sex, and sexual violence.

blocks.text: Jing Zou’s captivating debut feature, an intimate, decade-spanning character study, explores the consequences of the single-child policy on generations of Chinese girls.
Oscar nominee Cynthia Erivo gives a captivating central performance in Susanna White’s much-anticipated screen adaptation of Suzie Miller’s globally acclaimed play.
In Guy Nattiv’s tense, probing film, two young women attempt to extract their mother from a cult, but find themselves susceptible to its mysterious leader.
